seoTitle: Resize and Reset TradingView Charts to Default
metaDescription: Learn how to resize a TradingView chart by dragging its borders and how to quickly reset the view back to default with a right-click or double-click.
intro: It takes about two scroll-wheel nudges and one accidental drag to turn a clean TradingView chart into an unreadable mess of squeezed candles and an off-screen price axis. Instead of manually re-scaling everything, TradingView builds in two shortcuts that undo almost any layout mistake: a right-click reset that restores the chart's default zoom and scale, and a border-drag system for resizing panels on purpose. This guide walks through both, using a live US30 chart to show exactly where the reset option lives and what a resized chart looks like before and after.

steps.heading: Open the chart you want to adjust
steps.body: Start from any chart in your TradingView layout — in this walkthrough it's the Dow Jones Industrial Average (US30) on the 1D timeframe, with the watchlist docked on the right and volume and RSI panels stacked below the price chart. Nothing needs to be selected first; the reset and resize tools work on whichever chart currently has focus. If your layout has zoomed in tight enough that the candles are stretched wide and the recent price action has scrolled off to one side, that's exactly the state these shortcuts are built to fix.

image.caption: A US30 daily chart with the watchlist panel open on the right and volume and RSI indicators stacked underneath — a typical layout before anything gets resized or reset.

steps.heading: Right-click the chart to open the context menu
steps.body: Right-click anywhere on the price area of the chart, not on the toolbar or the watchlist. This opens a context menu with chart-specific actions: copying the price under your cursor, pasting, adding an alert or a trade order at that price level, adjusting drawings, and — near the top — Reset chart view, with its own keyboard shortcut listed next to it. That shortcut is the one to remember if you find yourself doing this often, since it saves opening the menu at all.

image.caption: The right-click context menu on a TradingView chart, with Reset chart view listed at the top alongside its keyboard shortcut.

steps.heading: Click Reset chart view
steps.body: Selecting Reset chart view snaps the chart back to its default zoom level and time range, centering the most recent candles and restoring the price axis to a normal scale. This only touches the visual framing — it doesn't delete drawings, remove indicators, or change any of your underlying settings, so it's a safe first move whenever a chart looks off after scrolling or zooming. It's the fastest fix for the most common complaint: you zoomed in to inspect a candle and now can't find your way back out.

image.caption: The same chart after a reset, showing a wider time range with the moving averages, volume bars, and RSI panel back in their normal proportions.

steps.heading: Resize a chart by dragging its border
steps.body: When you actually want a different size on purpose — more room for the price panel, less for volume — hover over the border between two panels or between the chart and the watchlist until the cursor changes to a resize arrow, then click and drag. Dragging the line between the price chart and the RSI panel below it, for example, gives the candles more vertical space at the expense of the indicator panel. This is manual and intentional, unlike the reset shortcut, so use it when you want to keep the new proportions rather than go back to default.

image.caption: A chart resized by dragging its border, giving the price panel more vertical room while volume and RSI compress underneath.

steps.heading: Double-click a border to snap it back
steps.body: If a manual resize doesn't look right, double-click the same border you dragged and TradingView returns that panel to its original size instantly, without needing to eyeball the drag a second time. This is a narrower tool than Reset chart view — it only affects panel proportions, not zoom or time range — so use it specifically when a resize, not a zoom, is what you want to undo.

steps.heading: Know which shortcut fixes which problem
steps.body: It's worth keeping these two straight since they solve different problems: Reset chart view (right-click menu or its shortcut) fixes zoom and scroll position, while double-clicking a border fixes panel size. If a chart looks wrong after you've been scrolling and zooming, reach for reset first. If it looks wrong because you dragged a panel border too far, double-click that border instead. Neither one touches your indicators, drawings, or saved chart data — they're purely visual, which makes them safe to use freely while you're finding a layout that works.

faq.question: How do I reset a TradingView chart to default?
faq.answer: Right-click the chart and select Reset chart view to restore the default zoom level and time range.

faq.question: How can I resize a chart?
faq.answer: Hover over the border between two panels — or between the chart and the watchlist — until the cursor changes, then click and drag to resize.

faq.question: Is there a shortcut to undo a resize?
faq.answer: Yes, double-clicking the same border you dragged instantly returns that panel to its original size.

faq.question: Will resetting the chart delete my data?
faq.answer: No, Reset chart view only restores zoom and scale. It doesn't remove indicators, drawings, or any saved chart data.

faq.question: Does this work for any asset type?
faq.answer: Yes — these reset and resize shortcuts are part of the chart interface itself, so they work the same way regardless of what symbol or asset is loaded.
